title: Scam or safe message cards
subject: PSHE
source: Written for pshe/y9 lesson 7 (Scam or safe message cards (pupil PDF, invented))
intro: Lesson 7: Scams and staying safe with money. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Common scams
points: Fake online shops and too-good deals

panels.title: Warning signs
points: Asks for bank details or codes
Pay by bank transfer or gift card only

panels.title: Money mules
points: Can mean a criminal record and losing your bank account

model.title: Text: 'Your parcel is held. Pay £1.45 here: bit.ly/xyz'

parts.text: Check: no parcel expected; the link is not the courier's site

head: Message
Scam or safe?
Reason
rows: Text: 'Your parcel is held. Pay £1.45 to release it: bit.ly/pay-now'
Email from your school: 'Reminder: the science homework is on the portal.' No links to log in.
DM: 'Earn £500 a week! Just let money go through your bank account.'
Text: 'Your bank: we will never ask for your PIN. Your new card has been posted.'
Pop-up: 'You've WON a phone! Enter your card details to pay postage in 10 minutes.'
Online shop: trainers usually £120, now £15, pay by bank transfer only.
Message from 'Mum' on a new number: 'Lost my phone, send £200 now, don't call.'
Text from your dentist: 'Appointment Tue 3 pm. Reply Y to confirm.'

blocks.answers: 1) Scam: unexpected, urgent, short link. Do not click; forward to 7726. 2) Safe: expected, no request for details or money. 3) Scam: money muling, a crime. 4) Safe: information only, asks for nothing (still check in the bank's app). 5) Scam: prize you did not enter, pressure, asks for card details. 6) Scam: too good to be true, unusual payment method. 7) Scam: urgent, secret, new number. Call Mum on her usual number. 8) Safe: expected and asks for nothing (check if unsure).

keywords.def: a trick to steal money or information
a crime of deceiving people for money
someone who lets criminals move money through their account (a crime)
the UK's national reporting centre for fraud

questions.q: Spot three warning signs: 'Congrats! You've won an iPhone. Pay £2 delivery in the next 10 minutes.'
questions.a: Unexpected prize, pressure (10 minutes), payment for a 'free' prize.

questions.q: Core: Scam or safe? (pupil PDF): judge eight messages and give a reason for each.
Extend: In the portal response box, write advice for an older relative about phone scams.
questions.a: Banks never ask for PINs; hang up and call the bank on a known number; tell family.

questions.q: Someone online offers £300 to 'receive and send on' money through your account. This is...
questions.a: B) Money muling, a crime. It moves criminal money; the account holder can be prosecuted.

questions.q: To report a scam text in the UK, forward it to... A) 999 B) 7726 C) 111
Big question: why would a scammer want a teenager's bank account?
questions.a: To move stolen money (money mule), which is a crime.
